diagnostic_evidence.quote:
The left-hand side is a coercive operator, thus
  $\varphi^{n+\theta}=\varphi^{n}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The form contains only gradients, so every nonzero constant has zero quadratic form and nonzero H1 norm. It is therefore not coercive on H1. The later deduction of equality of potentials also only determines their gradients unless a boundary condition, quotient space, or gauge normalization is imposed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State and use a coercive potential space, such as an appropriate H1_0 space, or work modulo constants and normalize the potential; adjust the preservation conclusion accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted semidiscrete well-posedness and exact preservation of the potential are not established as stated; potentials are at best determined up to constants.
issues.title: The semidiscrete bilinear form is not coercive on H1
issues.why_classification: A standard boundary condition or gauge restriction locally removes the constant kernel without changing the scheme's substantive conclusions.

issues.failure_explanation: Membership in L-infinity does not imply nonnegativity. For example, with zero magnetic field and a sufficiently large negative constant density, the quadratic form is a negative multiple of the gradient norm. Thus even after removing the constant kernel, coercivity does not follow from the stated hypothesis.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that the density is nonnegative, preferably bounded below by a positive constant if that is required elsewhere.
issues.overall_effect: The well-posedness and drift-compatibility argument lack a stated hypothesis needed for the elliptic operator to be positive.
issues.title: Semidiscrete coercivity omits the required positivity of density
issues.why_classification: The paper already works with positive admissible densities, so adding the omitted local hypothesis preserves the advertised regime and conclusions.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed lower bound treats both density-weighted terms as nonnegative, but the proposition assumes only mesh regularity and imposes no sign condition on the nodal density. Negative nodal density can make these terms negative and invalidate the claimed bound.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
compute $\widetilde \varphi_h^{n+1}\in\mathbb H_h$
  satisfying the discrete Gauß law

\mathbb H_h &:= \{ \psi_h \in \mathcal C^0(\domain) \;:\; \psi_h \circ
  \vec T_K \in \mathbb Q_1 \text{ for all } K \in \mathcal T_h \}.

issues.failure_explanation: The constant function 1 belongs to the stated space. Testing with it gives zero on the left but alpha times the positive total mass on the right. Hence the restart problem has no solution for the positive densities considered in the paper unless boundary-restricted test spaces or a compatible Neumann formulation are supplied.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify Dirichlet boundary data and use the corresponding homogeneous test space, or formulate compatible Neumann data together with the necessary compatibility condition and gauge.
issues.overall_effect: The full restart and the later relaxation restart are not defined by the displayed equation, and estimates involving its purported solution are not applicable as written.
issues.title: The full Gauss-law restart equation is inconsistent on the stated test space
issues.why_classification: A standard boundary-space specification locally restores solvability and is consistent with the homogeneous Dirichlet treatment used in the numerical section.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Assume that the hyperbolic update is at least first-order accurate in
  time and space and subject to a hyperbolic CFL condition $\tau_n =
  \mathcal O(h)$.

A more careful
  analysis for the case $\theta=1/2$ establishes the improved result
  $\mathcal O(h^3+h^{1+s})$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof explicitly leaves its key comparison between the actual split density and a formal theta-scheme density unverified. First-order accuracy and a CFL relation alone do not provide the stated uniform operator-norm estimate without regularity, stability, consistency-norm, and splitting-error arguments. The improved third-order local residual estimate is merely asserted.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must define the operator norm, state sufficient solution and method regularity assumptions, and prove the local density/splitting estimates for the concrete hyperbolic and source updates.
issues.overall_effect: Neither residual rate in the proposition nor the accumulated restart and energy-error rates in the corollary are established.
issues.title: Gauss-law residual convergence rates are asserted without sufficient assumptions or proof
issues.why_classification: The missing step is the central nontrivial estimate of the proposition, and the source supplies neither assumptions nor an argument from which the claimed rates can be recovered.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
This can be achieved via an artificial relaxation approach by lowering the
kinetic energy appropriately

issues.failure_explanation: If the kinetic energy is zero, the quotient is undefined. If the positive field-energy increase exceeds the available kinetic energy, the factor inside the square root is negative. No hypothesis or fallback excludes either case. Moreover, in the excess-energy case momentum relaxation alone cannot compensate the restart's full energy increase.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add and verify conditions ensuring positive kinetic energy and 0 <= delta E <= Ekin, or provide a different fallback that handles zero or insufficient kinetic energy while preserving the required admissibility and energy properties.
issues.overall_effect: The proposed energy-restoring restart is not a real-valued, executable update for all states in its stated scope and does not generally reestablish the promised energy balance.
issues.title: The relaxation restart can take the square root of a negative or undefined quantity
issues.why_classification: A simple formula edit cannot retain the unconditional energy-restoration promise; a conditional restriction or an additional relaxation mechanism is required.
